misclassified_entities.original_description: External source code using mnemonic opcode names
misclassified_entities.reason_for_misclassification: Contract source code is not an external entity but an input data artifact. The actual external entity would be the developer or tool submitting source code for compilation. Source code itself is data, not an actor.
Bytecode is data stored on-chain, not an external entity that sends data into the system. The external entity would be the contract creator who deployed the bytecode or the caller invoking it.

misclassified_entities.original_description: SYSTEM_ADDRESS (0xfff...ffe) used as origin for system calls
misclassified_entities.reason_for_misclassification: SYSTEM_ADDRESS is a protocol-defined constant address used internally for system transaction origin. It's not an external entity - it's an internal protocol mechanism. No external party controls this address.

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: The contract or EOA that invoked the ECRECOVER precompile
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Any contract or EOA can call the ECRECOVER precompile at address 0x01. The caller provides signature data (message hash, v, r, s) which could be malicious, invalid, or crafted to exploit signature malleability. The extensive validation (v check, r/s range checks, curve bounds) exists precisely because callers are untrusted.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - precompile accessible to any caller

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Validator or consensus client that produces and proposes blocks
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Block producers in Proof-of-Stake are staked validators who have economic incentive to behave honestly. However, they control block content and could attempt invalid state transitions. All block data (headers, transactions, state roots) must be fully validated - the extensive validation checks (gas limits, base fee, state root, receipt root, gas used) exist because even staked validators cannot be fully trusted.

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: External user or application that submits transactions
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Transaction submitters are anonymous network participants. The extensive transaction validation (gas checks, blob gas, ECDSA recovery, fee validation, nonce matching, balance checks, EOA verification) exists because transaction submitters are completely untrusted. Any entity can submit transactions attempting to drain accounts, exploit contracts, or cause DoS.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: ECDSA signature (proves private key ownership, not identity)

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Consensus layer providing withdrawal and deposit information
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: The beacon chain is a separate consensus layer with its own security model. Data from the beacon chain (withdrawals, deposits, beacon roots) is validated by the consensus layer before reaching the execution layer. However, the execution layer still validates withdrawal amounts and formats because cross-layer trust boundaries exist.

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Entity that deployed the contract bytecode being analyzed
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Contract deployers can deploy arbitrary bytecode including malicious code. The jump destination analysis exists because deployed bytecode cannot be trusted - it could contain crafted sequences attempting to jump into PUSH data or invalid locations. All bytecode is analyzed to identify valid JUMPDEST locations regardless of deployer.

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: External account or contract initiating the message call
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Message callers can invoke any contract with arbitrary calldata. The EVM validates jump targets during execution because callers could attempt to trigger jumps to invalid destinations. The caller controls the target address and call data but cannot bypass runtime jump validation.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - any account can make calls

boundary_edges.data_flow_description: Caller provides signature data (hash, v, r, s) for ECDSA recovery
Block producer proposes block for state transition processing
Transaction submitter sends signed transaction for validation and execution
Beacon chain provides withdrawal and deposit requests for processing
Deployed bytecode received for jump destination analysis
External caller initiates message call with target and calldata

coverage_analysis.notes: Prague ECRECOVER (spec_6df40d28991fc4b884a4e879a849708d3fbfbc88) has comprehensive signature validation including v range (27/28), r/s range checks against SECP256K1N, and signature malleability considerations. Prague Fork (spec_7075bc8602661016a3bc37ec02958b96b2d92f66) is a large specification covering block state transitions, transaction processing, gas economics, system transactions, and request processing - extensive validation at every layer reflects untrusted nature of inputs. EIP-1803 (spec_745fa89a207e4a2ae7cc49148094f1aa3d19e61d) is a cosmetic opcode renaming EIP with no runtime security implications - hex values unchanged. Prague Runtime (spec_7bbe2c915f8c3ef975b0bbe2f0e7f503e03c3e29) covers jump destination validation - critical security mechanism preventing arbitrary code execution from PUSH data. EIP-5656 MCOPY (spec_7ead572e3fd23654df5b56b843b97020203c1631) has no external entities - it's an internal memory operation with gas-based DoS protection and safe overlap handling semantics.
